headline: Govt employees' new pay scale approved, basic salary to rise by 100-142%
summary: The new 2026 pay scale will be implemented in four stages, with basic salaries increasing significantly for both new and existing employees.
details: The government has approved a new pay scale for 2026, with basic salaries increasing by 100 to 142 percent across different grades. The implementation will take place in four stages, effective from July.

For grades 1 to 9, the first stage of the increase will be 40% of the new basic salary, effective from July. A further 30% will be added in January 2027, and the remaining 30% will the effective from July 2027.

An employee joining in the 9th grade in July of this year with a basic salary of 22,000 BDT, will see their basic salary rise to 30,800 BDT in the first stage, then to 37,400 BDT in January 2027, and finally to 44,000 BDT by July 2027.

New allowance rates will be new effective from January 1, 2028, while previous allowances will remain in place until then. For a 9th grade officer in Dhaka, the total salary and allowances could reach approximately 70,000 BDT.

The overall maximum basic salary for the 9th grade can reach 1.05 lakh BDT through increments. The Finance Division will soon issue a formal government order to clarify the exact salary details for new and old employees.
Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani confirmed that the Finance Division is likely to issue the order today or tomorrow.

headline_marked: 12 injured as [[clash erupts at Bogura hospital]] over patient death
headline: 12 injured as clash erupts at Bogura hospital over patient death
summary: Intern doctors at Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College Hospital are on strike after a violent altercation with a patient's relatives.
details: At least 12 people, including six intern doctors, were injured in a clash between the relatives of a deceased patient and intern doctors at Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College Hospital in Bogura.
The incident occurred around 11:00 PM last night following the death of a patient who had been suffering from prolonged respiratory problems, according to hospital authorities.
Relatives alleged the patient died due to a wrong injection, leading to an altercation that turned violent. They further claimed that some relatives were confined and beaten by the interns.

Police reported that relatives initially attacked the doctors over negligence allegations. In response, interns confined and assaulted some of the relatives, leading to police to take four people into custody.
Hospital authorities denied the allegation of medical negligence, stating the patient had long-term respiratory issues. Three of the six injured intern doctors suffered serious injuries.
Intern doctors have launched an indefinite work abstention since midnight, demanding that those involved in the attack be brought to justice.
